Subject: Checkout failures + latency spikes (HOLIDAY promotion window)

Can you escalate to engineering/ops and get an ETA? We need either a short-term mitigation or a rollback option within the hour.

Subject: Re: Checkout failures + latency spikes (HOLIDAY promotion window)

Quick triage (initial):
- Observed sustained queueing on the inference pool handling Clearline traffic from 08:42–09:08 ET.
- Concurrency cap applied at pod level: 64 in-flight requests. When token-heavy requests surge, we see head-of-line blocking as long requests occupy slots.
- Significant KV cache cold-miss rate for that rollout group (~48% miss rate in the samples attached). Misses correlate with long-tail p99 increases.
- A subset of requests returned 503s when backend connection pool exhausted (we're seeing transient connection resets).

Attachments: kvcache-metrics-20271110.csv (sampled misses + latency bins)
Link to trace: https://app.redwood.internal/traces/trace-9a8b

Proposed short-term mitigations (<= 2 hours):
1) Temporarily increase concurrency cap on the affected pool from 64 -> 96 for Clearline routing (low-risk, short duration).
2) Enable priority routing for short-checkout-path requests to avoid head-of-line blocking.
3) Pre-warm KV cache for common prefixes for 15 minutes using synthetic warmers.
4) If (1-3) insufficient, authorize a fast capacity bump (add one GPU shard to the Dedicated pool) — requires Marcus sign-off.

I'll continue to collect flame graphs and check whether the connection pool reset rate correlates to a particular host.

-David
David Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Leadership <leadership@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:50:00 -0500
Subject: Executive note — Clearline checkout impact and requested short-term override

Folks — looping in execs since Clearline represents a high-revenue Q4 customer and the promotion window is active. Summary:
- Customer experiencing p99 latency spike and ~12% 503s during peak promotion traffic.
- Root causes: request packing (token-heavy inputs) -> head-of-line queueing; elevated KV cache miss rate; connection pool exhaustion on a small subset of workers.

Options and ask (fast decision required):
A) Approve temporary concurrency cap override for Clearline routing (64->96) for 3 hours. Estimated incremental cost: ~$1,100 for the window. Low-risk rollback.
B) Approve adding 1 GPU shard to their Dedicated pool for 24 hours to restore headroom. Cost estimate: ~$3,500. Requires account finance sign-off but can be done under emergency credit.
C) Refuse and require application-level rollback; risk of customer churn / SLA breach.

Recommend option A immediately, and prepare option B if A insufficient. Requesting quick approval from Execs — please reply with A or B by 10:15 ET.

Marcus Lin
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@clearline-retail.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Checkout failures + latency spikes (HOLIDAY promotion window)

Liam — sincerely sorry for the disruption. We're executing a mitigation plan now, timeline below: 
- 10:06 ET: Enabled priority routing for checkout-step requests to reduce HL blocking (monitoring).
- 10:08 ET: Started KV cache pre-warm job for the top 500 prefixes — expected effect within ~10 minutes.
- 10:12 ET: Temporarily increased concurrency cap for Clearline from 64 -> 96 (3 hour window) — Marcus authorized.
- 10:25 ET: Monitoring shows 503 rate falling from 12% -> 3% and p99 improving by ~420ms.

Next steps:
- We'll run a short synthetic acceptance test at 10:40 and share detailed post-mortem tomorrow.
- Attaching a mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-CL-78.pdf) with timings and RACI.

Subject: Re: Checkout failures + latency spikes (HOLIDAY promotion window) — resolution and next steps

Liam — following up with the final update and next steps.

What we did
- Short-term: increased concurrency cap for Clearline routing, applied priority routing for checkout, pre-warmed KV caches, and monitored connection pool resets. Those actions reduced the 503 rate to <1% and brought p99 back near baseline within ~30 minutes.
- Exec-approved: we provisioned a 24-hour Dedicated shard as a precautionary buffer; finance will bill per the CL-78 emergency credit.

Why it happened (summary)
- A concentrated burst of token-heavy requests during the promotion caused long-inference requests to occupy slots (head-of-line blocking). At the same time, a recent rollout had higher KV cache miss rates which amplified per-request latency. Connection resets on a small subset of workers worsened the transient 503s.

Follow-ups (owners & timeline)
- Post-mortem doc with timelines, root cause artifacts, and long-term mitigations (David) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Patch: implement token-length based routing guard and increase default pool cap for high-throughput accounts (Engineering roadmap item) — Marcus to prioritize in next sprint.
- Customer: Hannah to schedule a debrief with Clearline and coordinate a joint test before the next promotion.

We appreciate the quick coordination — please reach out if you'd like a walkthrough of the post-mortem or the KV pre-warm plan.

Best,
Sofia
